UnitStatement: Deliverable DEL-08-04 'Result export format' belongs to package PKG-08 (Reporting, Audit, and Reproducibility).
DEL-08-04 deliverable type is API_CONTRACT under scope item SOW-046.
DEL-08-04 supports objectives OBJ-007 and OBJ-009.
DEL-08-04 is a draft setup artifact, not an implementation.
The primary artifact is a machine-readable result export contract for review, regression comparison, and downstream tooling.
The baseline export format is schema-first JSON result envelopes.
Additional export formats (CSV, HDF5, neutral-file, spreadsheet, external tool formats) are TBD and not chosen as final by this setup deliverable.
Anticipated implementation artifacts are schemas/results.schema.yaml, exporter source, and tests, not created in this setup session.
Envelope content categories: result identity, model/run references, unit-aware value arrays, diagnostics, provenance, analysis status, warnings, and reproducibility references.
Exports support review and comparison; they do not certify, seal, approve, authenticate, or declare code compliance.
Exported values must be unit-aware and dimensionally traceable; missing units are findings, not silent defaults.
Public export contracts must not embed protected standards text, copied standards tables, proprietary formulas, private rule-pack payloads, or private project data by default.
This session is setup/document production only; no schema file, exporter source, tests, or repository-level artifacts are modified.
The export baseline is a JSON result envelope contract; any additional export format remains TBD until a later bounded decision or implementation brief.
Result exports must preserve the PKG-00 no-bypass baseline: adapters and downstream tools cannot bypass unit checks, diagnostics, provenance, data boundaries, or professional-responsibility notices.
Mechanics results, user-rule-check results, and human review/approval states must remain distinguishable in exported data.
Exported diagnostics must carry enough structured information for review and regression triage without relying on prose-only warnings.
Result envelope header identifies export schema version, result set ID, model/run reference, solver version reference, and creation context, without implying validation or certification.
Unit-aware result payloads carry displacement, rotation, force, moment, reaction, stress, ratio, or rule-check values with unit metadata and dimensional categories, with no hidden unit defaults.
Diagnostics block carries structured diagnostics with code, class, severity, source, affected object, message, remediation, and provenance, and must not be dropped by exporters or adapters.

Provenance and reproducibility references link to model hash, manifest, rule-pack checksum, source notes, and input/run identifiers without copying protected or private payloads into public artifacts.
Analysis status fields distinguish MECHANICS_SOLVED, RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE, USER_RULE_CHECKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, and must not emit automatic CODE_COMPLIANT or professional approval status.
Regression comparison surface provides stable identifiers, deterministic ordering, and numeric/unit metadata suitable for comparison tests.
Downstream tooling handoff provides a stable machine-readable contract for headless CLI, report generation, GUI results viewer, and adapters; non-JSON formats remain TBD.
The result export format makes solver and rule-check outputs reviewable, reproducible, comparable, and consumable by downstream tools without losing code-neutral project boundaries.
Preserve the result envelope as the governed contract; downstream tools may consume exports but should not bypass unit checks, diagnostics, provenance, data handling, or report controls.
Keep the export format review-oriented; the software must not claim certification, sealing, approval, authentication, or automatic code compliance.
Treat units as data, not context; every exported numeric result needs explicit unit and dimensional meaning, or a diagnostic explaining why it is incomplete.
Keep diagnostics structured with stable diagnostic codes, classes, severities, and affected-object references rather than prose-only warnings.
Carry reproducibility references (model hashes, manifest IDs, solver versions, rule-pack checksums) without copying private payloads such as protected text, proprietary formulas, or owner data.
Prefer deterministic ordering and stable identifiers for regression comparison.
Use TBD for unresolved format decisions; do not imply a spreadsheet, CSV, FEA handoff, or other external export has been selected.
Start from JSON result envelopes because they align with the architecture basis and can be validated before exporter code exists.
Exports are machine-readable result contracts; reports are human-facing review artifacts that may consume exports but keep their own wording and protected-content controls.
Mechanics result values and user-rule-check outcomes should remain separately identifiable; a user-rule check is not professional approval.
Export consumers should be able to filter diagnostics by class, severity, source, affected object, remediation, and provenance.
Stable object identifiers, result-station identifiers, load-case/combination references, deterministic ordering, and unit metadata matter more than display formatting for regression comparison.
Downstream tools need a governed envelope first; concrete external formats and transport protocols are later decisions.
Public fixtures should use invented or permissively licensed data only; user-private exports remain user controlled and should not become public defaults.
Use the single JSON envelope as the baseline; additional formats remain TBD to avoid premature commitments and governance bypasses.
Preserve units, diagnostics, provenance, and status semantics even when compactness is desirable; reviewability takes precedence over minimal payload size.
Include stable machine identifiers for comparison and tooling; human-readable labels may supplement but not replace them.
Export identifiers, versions, checksums, source notes, and redistribution status; do not copy private formulas or protected values into public artifacts.
Avoid report/export wording that could be read as approval or compliance; human review remains external to the software result.

A displacement result should be a unit-aware value with node/result reference, load-case or combination basis, and source run metadata; a value without unit metadata or affected-object reference is unacceptable.

A rule-check outcome should carry rule-pack ID/version/checksum and a status distinguishing incomplete inputs, checked, or failed; automatic CODE_COMPLIANT status or copied protected formula text is unacceptable.

A warning should be a structured diagnostic with class, severity, source, affected object, message, remediation, and provenance; a prose-only warning that cannot be traced or compared is unacceptable.

A downstream export adapter should consume the governed JSON envelope and preserve units, provenance, and diagnostics; an adapter shortcut that drops diagnostics or private-data handling is unacceptable.
No unresolved source conflicts were found during this setup run; open format choices remain TBD by scope, not as a source conflict.

The deliverable defines the setup specification for a machine-readable result export contract with a schema-first JSON result envelope baseline for review, regression comparison, and downstream tooling.
The setup run does not implement exporter code, edit schemas/results.schema.yaml, create tests, finalize additional export formats, or modify documentation outside the deliverable folder.
DEL-08-04-R1: The result export baseline shall be a schema-first JSON result envelope.
DEL-08-04-R2: Additional concrete export formats shall remain TBD unless later approved and scoped; this deliverable shall not finalize CSV, spreadsheet, FEA, HDF5, or other external formats.
DEL-08-04-R3: Result envelopes shall preserve units and dimensional metadata for exported values and shall not rely on hidden unit defaults.

DEL-08-04-R4: Result envelopes shall carry or reference provenance and reproducibility metadata including model/run identity, solver version basis, rule-pack checksum, warnings, assumptions, and source notes.
DEL-08-04-R5: Result envelopes shall carry structured diagnostics using PKG-00 baseline fields: code, class, severity, source, affected object, message, remediation, and provenance.
DEL-08-04-R6: Exported statuses shall distinguish mechanics solved, user-rule checked, rule-input incomplete, human-review required, and human-approved record states where present.
DEL-08-04-R7: Result exports shall not claim certification, sealing, professional approval, authentication, or automatic engineering code compliance.

DEL-08-04-R8: Result exports and public examples shall not embed protected standards text, copied standards tables, proprietary formulas, private rule-pack payloads, or private project data by default.
DEL-08-04-R9: Exporters and adapters shall not bypass validation, unit checks, diagnostics, provenance handling, report controls, or public/private data-boundary checks.
DEL-08-04-R10: Export ordering and identifiers should be deterministic enough for regression comparison of equivalent result sets.
DEL-08-04-R11: Missing solve-required, rule-check-required, provenance, or unit metadata shall be represented as diagnostics/findings, not silently filled with defaults.

DEL-08-04-R12: The contract shall support downstream consumption by report generation, GUI results review, headless automation, and import/export adapters without creating a bypass around governed result envelopes.
JSON Schema 2020-12 is the baseline schema technology for public result envelope contracts.
A schema-first command/query/job result envelope baseline is required by the PKG-00 architecture basis as the result export/API boundary and no-bypass contract.
Canonical JSON / JCS-compatible canonicalization is relevant when exported JSON payloads or manifests are hashed for reproducibility; this deliverable shall preserve compatible references.
The OpenPipeStress invariant catalog provides IP, data, units, rule-pack, privacy, professional-responsibility, and agent-boundary constraints as binding project governance draft.
No protected engineering code, standard clause text, standards table, commercial example, or proprietary rule content is used as an authority in this setup artifact.
V-1: Validating a representative JSON result envelope against the result schema should pass and have required envelope fields present.
V-2: Exporting unit-bearing displacements, rotations, forces, moments, reactions, stresses, and ratios should give each value family explicit unit/dimensional metadata or a blocking diagnostic.
V-3: Exporting a run with missing rule-pack input or provenance should include structured diagnostics/findings instead of silent defaults.
V-4: Exporting a run with rule-pack references should record rule-pack identity/version/checksum/source status without copying private formulas or protected values.
V-5: Re-exporting an equivalent result set should produce stable identifiers and ordering allowing deterministic regression comparison.
V-6: Routing the export through an adapter or downstream tool should preserve unit, provenance, diagnostics, and professional-boundary fields.
V-7: Scanning public fixtures/templates should show protected/private data and certification/compliance claims are absent or blocked.
V-8: Generating a report or GUI result view from the export should let the consumer distinguish mechanics, user-rule, diagnostics, and human-review-required statuses.
The setup deliverable produces Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, Procedure.md, _SEMANTIC.md, _SEMANTIC_LENSING.md, Dependencies.csv, _DEPENDENCIES.md, run records, and _STATUS.md.
Future implementation artifacts anticipated by the register are schemas/results.schema.yaml, exporter source, and tests, not created or edited in this setup session.
